text:
maya: Heads up — got a DSAR deletion request from an EU user who says copies of their data may be in backups. They want full deletion and proof. How are we handling backups + retention exceptions? :eyes:

samir: Thanks. Two quick things: 1) we don't delete backups immediately; we rely on retention windows + legal holds. 2) for DSARs that require carving backups we need an approved retention-exception + documented workflow. I'll outline a runbook shortly.

alisa: We also need to consider who can request/perform the backup carve. Current RBAC prohibits bulk backup access for engineers. If we do a temporary exception we should use a short-lived role and mandatory audit logs that include KMS key IDs.

paul: +1. Proposed flow: create a JT ticket with reason + scope, @legal signoff, then ops runs a sandboxed restore into a disposable workspace, run deletion scripts, attach logs. No direct write access to production backups.

maya: That matches my thinking. Questions: a) how do we surface KMS usage in logs (key id, decrypt operations)? b) can we verify WORM/snapshot immutability before we trigger restore?

alisa: For KMS: our Cloud KMS audit logs include CryptoKey versions and the resource name. We need to ensure log retention long enough to provide proof to the requester (export as signed artifact). Example GCP audit filter we can use: `resource.type=\"kms_key\" protoPayload.methodName:\"Decrypt\"` 

samir: For AWS KMS it's CloudTrail events: `eventName=Decrypt` and CloudTrail records the KMS key ARN. We should export a signed digest (hash + timestamp) of the log slice we provide.

dsar-bot: Automated checklist: 1) Validate identity 2) Check for active legal hold 3) Request retention-exception if backups affected 4) Perform restore in disposable env 5) Run deletion script + verify 6) Provide audit bundle. See /policies/dsar for templates.

paul: Regarding RBAC changes: suggest a short-lived AWS IAM role `redwood:dsar-backup-access` assumed via SSO with expiration 6h, scoped to specific buckets/snapshots. All assume events must be recorded to central audit cluster and tied to ticket ID.

maya: Good. Legal question: can we redact instead of delete if logs/snapshots are shared with third parties? @legal any constraints?

legal: Short answer: if data has been shared with third parties we must try to get them to delete or prove they can't. If they can't, we need to document mitigation and inform the user. For backups, we need to document efforts and provide a statement of what we were able to delete vs. retain. We'll sign off on retention-exception templates.

alisa: One more operational detail: snapshots created by the hypervisor might reference underlying blocks we can't selectively zero. For block-level immutability we'll need to provide a technical statement describing why full physical deletion isn't feasible and what we did (logical deletion + access termination). Keep that in the audit bundle.

samir: I'll draft the JT ticket template + RBAC change template now. It will include: scope (snapshot IDs), justification, legal signoff checkbox, SRE approver, expiration TTL, and audit export path.

maya: Perfect. I'll start the DSAR intake and flag this as "backup-affected". Will link JT ticket here once created. :thumbsup:

paul: If anyone wants the initial proof artifact format, here's a minimal manifest we can include in the bundle:

```
manifest_version: 1
request_id: JT-12345
subject_id_hash: <sha256>
actions: [restore, run-delete, verify]
kms_key_ids: [projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/phi/cryptoKeys/phi-v1]
log_slice_path: gs://redwood-dsar-bundles/JT-12345/logs.tar.gz
verification_hash: <sha256-of-logs>
```

maya: This is great. Once JT-12345 is in place, ops and legal can coordinate. Thanks everyone.

samir: I'll post the templates in #eng-security/docs after I finish. Expect them in ~1h.

dsar-bot: Reminder: please attach user identity proof to the ticket and redact PII from logs before uploading to external storage.
